Systemic Lupus Erythematosus is a disease that can cause a wide range of symptoms, including hypertension, anemia, and pericardial effusion, due to autoimmune inflammation and deposition of immune complexes.
Hypertensive Heart Disease is a condition that can cause cardiac damage and dysfunction due to prolonged high blood pressure, leading to symptoms such as orthopnea and fatigue.
Pericarditis is an inflammation of the pericardium that can cause pericardial effusion and cardiac tamponade, leading to symptoms such as chest pain and shortness of breath.
Chronic Kidney Disease is a condition that can cause anemia and hypertension due to decreased kidney function, leading to symptoms such as fatigue and shortness of breath.
